title: Making data protection depend on employees remembering the rules
summary: Make approved data handling understandable and supported by technical controls across the information lifecycle.
diagnosis: Data protection can fail at input, retrieval, output, logs, persistent memory or sharing—not only when someone forgets to remove a name. Identify the permitted purpose and audience at each stage. Account settings and contracts matter, but they need to be connected to an approved working path that people can actually use.
diagnostic_questions: Which services and accounts receive company information, and who has checked their permitted use and retention arrangements?
Can sensitive information move from a legitimate read into an inappropriate output, trace or shared memory?
Are collection, access, retention, correction and deletion responsibilities assigned?
proposed_actions: Classify the data and approved purposes for each workflow; provide supported accounts and connectors rather than rely on informal personal use.
Apply suitable access restrictions and automated input/output checks, and minimise what is retained in traces and memory.
Define retention and deletion processes with responsible specialists, then test the real data path—including logs, cached copies and downstream destinations.
working_artifact: Data-flow and lifecycle record: input; sensitivity; purpose; service/account; access; transformations; output recipients; logs; memory; retention; deletion/correction route; responsible owner.
measures: Coverage of live workflows by a reviewed data-flow record and approved service/account arrangement.
Detected leakage or overexposure in controlled tests and operational incidents, without exposing sensitive test data in dashboards.
Completion of retention, access-review and deletion obligations for the defined data population.
tradeoff: Removing names alone does not establish that information is non-sensitive. Local hosting and ownership also do not automatically make a system secure. Legal or contractual requirements depend on the actual use and jurisdiction and require appropriate specialist review; this page is not a compliance determination.
illustrative_case: Illustrative application: an assistant legitimately reads an employee record but must not include salary details in a broadly shared incident summary or retain them in an unrestricted debugging log.
